**Excess social media use in normal populations is associated with amygdala-striatal but not with prefrontal morphology** (URL: [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925492717302159](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925492717302159)) (No-sign-in URL: [https://www.scribd.com/document/833167695/Excess-Social-Media-Use-in-Normal-Populations-is-Associated-With-Amygdala-striatal-but-Not-Prefrontal-Morphology](https://www.scribd.com/document/833167695/Excess-Social-Media-Use-in-Normal-Populations-is-Associated-With-Amygdala-striatal-but-Not-Prefrontal-Morphology)) 

*(Published Sep 2017\)*

\*Important note about this study: compares relatively-low and relatively-high social media use groups’ brain GMV/morphology. However, researchers state neither group is at a level that would typically be considered “addicted” or extreme, meaning these findings are applicable for “normal”/”reasonable,” but frequent, social media use impacts. Useful information for project since most people will not be in an “addiction”-level category (especially because that is still not clinically defined/definitively proven\!)

* Study looks at 50 university students–25 in a case group w/ relatively high Excess Social Media Use (ESMU) scores, and 25 as a control w/ relatively low ESMU scores  
* ESMU was measured using a “14-item Facebook-specific adaption of the Compulsive Internet Use instrument, measured on a 1-5 Likert scale”  
    * Note that the researchers did not assign an “addicted” or “not-addicted” label based on this survey “given that such cutoffs are not formally defined,” but based on other research on video game use considered low ESMU as low-use, no-addiction, and high ESMU as no-addiction as well but much higher-use   
* Used structural MRI scans to analyze brain structure/volume via Voxel-Based Morphometry, and compare between the two groups

* Intro cites a study, [Bányai et al., 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5222338/), to claim that although there is no established clinical terminology/classification for excess social media use, “**most users present some degree of excess use and about 4.5% may be classified as at-risk for addiction**”   
    * May be useful to look into as well  
* Based on the dual system theory, stating “excess behaviors stem from an imbalance between hyperactivity of the reward system … and hypo-activity of the inhibition system,” researchers hypothesized ESMU may be associated with differences in gray matter volume (GMV) in regions of the brain responsible for reward system/inhibition system  
    * Specifically mention the bilateral amygdala, describing how mesolimbic-dopamine system is very morphologically flexible and as a result structural abnormalities in the amygdala “are associated with excess behaviors”  
    * Also hypothesize about ventral striatum (Nucleus Accumbens, abbreviated NAcc), writing that “it is a central reward hub that has been shown to be involved in many excess behaviors”   
    * About prefrontal cortex regions/brain’s executive control & inhibition functions, theorized that strong impact would not be seen due to “mixed findings” in previous research on Internet Addiction (IA) and less morphological flexibility in this region of the brain  
* Hypotheses above provide basis for aim of study & summary of previous research


* Analysis of the individuals’ MRI scans showed that the case group (**high ESMU-scoring individuals**) **had reduced GMV in the bilateral amygdala and right ventral striatum**, **but no differences in the prefrontal cortex**, compared to the control group (low ESMU-scoring individuals) 

![][image1]

* "In the figure above, diagrams A and B indicate in blue “voxel-wise VMB results,” green “anatomical ROIs used to extract GMV,” and light blue “overlapping regions”"  
    * "The horizontal axis in graphs C, D, and E represents individuals’ ESMU score, and the vertical axis (containing arbitrary values) shows the relative GMV in each region. Graph C is ESMU score vs. GMV in left amygdala, graph D is ESMU score vs. GMV in right amygdala, and graph E is ESMU score vs. GMV in right striatum"  
    * "The graphs F, G, and H similarly show the left amygdala, right amygdala, and right striatum GMV distribution (respectively) comparing between the relatively-low ESMU control group and relatively-high ESMU case group"  
* "Researchers discuss how **lack of differences in prefrontal morphology between the two groups** studied here **may indicate “potential differences between morphology in presumably normal populations with reasonable levels of ESMU and those who present very high levels of ESMU and often meet at-risk for addiction criteria”**  
* "Researchers provide **three possible explanations/interpretations** of this data, which study by itself cannot prove or disprove (it only showed association)"**:**  
1. **"People with lower GMV in amygdala/striatum may be more prone to excessive behaviors like ESMU**, since reward pathway may then respond to stimuli faster than inhibition/executive control brain regions intervene"  
2. **“Incentive-sensitization theory”**: suggests **that social media itself may influence amygdala-striatal system** (reward pathway), and this would involve “neural pruning, with the objective to produce a more efficient amygdala-striatal system that can deal with the growing reward processing demands (Kanai and Rees, 2011)”  
3. **"A common factor like genetics could exist that would both mean lower amygdala/striatum GMV"**, **and also “more flexible adaptations in response to changes in reward frequency and intensity** (Brewer and Potenza, 2008; Clark, 2002)”

   

* Limitations of study:  
    * Did not include individuals with extreme ESMU scores–only analyzed normal variation in population, comparing relatively lower and higher users of social media  
    * Data was cross-sectional, so could not establish causality relationship (see hypotheses/possible explanations in notes above)  
        * Authors suggest longitudinal studies in future to test these hypotheses
